snippet.title: Prompt Claude Like the Top 1% (in 30 Seconds).
snippet.description:
Wispr Flow → https://ref.wisprflow.ai/tristen-obrien-yt
(one month free)

Learn how to prompt Claude like the top 1% using your voice instead of typing. This video covers the 30 second rule for prompting Claude AI, the free Claude skill that runs it for you, and how to turn your meetings into prompts with Wispr Flow Notetaker.
---

WHY YOUR CLAUDE PROMPTS COME BACK GENERIC

Most people send Claude a four sentence prompt and then wonder why the answer feels generic. It is not the model. You did not tell it enough. Typing out everything you know about a project is miserable, so nobody does it.

In 30 seconds of typing, a fast typist gets maybe 20 words onto the screen. In 30 seconds of talking, you get around 70. Same half minute, three times the context. That is the entire trick, and it is why voice to text changes how good your prompts are.

---

WHAT'S IN THIS VIDEO

How to prompt Claude with your voice instead of typing
The 30 second rule for starting any project with Claude AI
Why more context beats clever prompt engineering tricks
How to make Claude ask you 5 questions before it writes anything
Using a voice to text tool on your computer and on your phone
Voice snippets and a custom dictionary for names and spellings
How to take AI meeting notes without a bot joining the call
Connecting Wispr Flow Notetaker to Claude with MCP

---

THE 30 SECOND RULE

Before you start any project with Claude, talk to it for at least 30 seconds first.

Dump everything in your head. Out of order is fine. Unfinished sentences are fine. Making sense of it is Claude's job.

Then tell it not to write anything yet, and to ask you at least five questions before it writes the prompt.

---

THE CLAUDE SKILL (free, copy this into Claude)

Create a skill called 30 Second Rule.

It should trigger any time I say I'm going to brain dump, that I'm about to dump everything, that I want to talk something through before we start, or any time I clearly start describing a new project in a long, unstructured, out-of-order way.

When it triggers, follow these steps exactly:

One. Do not write anything yet. Do not summarize what I said, do not start the task, do not offer suggestions. Let me finish talking.

Two. When I stop, ask me at least five questions, more if the project needs it. Only ask about things I genuinely did not cover. Never ask me something I already answered, and never ask me who you should be or what role to take. Focus the questions on what most changes the output: who the result is for, what format it needs, how deep it should go, what it must include, what to avoid, and how I'll know it's right. Ask them all at once as a numbered list.

Three. After I answer, analyze everything I've said and decide on your own what role or persona is best suited to do this job. Do not ask me. Then write a single, detailed, self-contained prompt that opens by assigning that persona, and includes every relevant detail from my brain dump and my answers, organized into clear sections. It should be specific enough that someone with no context could run it and get what I want.

Four. Output only that prompt, ready to run. Do not do the task itself unless I ask you to.

---
